title: Quantum superposition & measurement — external pre/post items

pre.prompt: A particle in an infinite potential well of width L is in the state ψA(x,0) = √(1/6)·φ0(x) + √(1/3)·φ1(x) + √(1/2)·φ2(x), where φn are the energy eigenfunctions with energies En. A single measurement of the energy is made. What is the probability that the result is E1?
pre.explanation: MIT 8.04 Spring 2013, Problem Set 4 solutions (3d): "the probability of measuring energy En is given by |cn|2" — here |c1|2 = (√(1/3))2 = 1/3. Answer key per https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/8-04-quantum-physics-i-spring-2013/resources/mit8_04s13_ps4_sol/

pre.prompt: For the same state ψA (a superposition of the energy eigenfunctions φ0, φ1 and φ2), a single measurement of the energy is made. What is the probability that the result equals the expectation value ⟨E⟩ of the energy in that state?
pre.explanation: MIT 8.04 Spring 2013, Problem Set 4 solutions (3c): "The probability of measuring an energy equal to (E^) is zero." Only the eigenvalues E0, E1, E2 of the superimposed eigenstates can be measured. Answer key per https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/8-04-quantum-physics-i-spring-2013/resources/mit8_04s13_ps4_sol/

pre.prompt: An understanding of the diffraction pattern associated with particles is based on
options: Forces that the De Broglie pilot wave exert on individual particles.
Interference between the component of the wave from each slit.
Forces that the De Broglie pilot wave exert between pairs of particles.
All of these nearly equivalent models explain diffraction.
The fact that particles can make glancing collisions with the edge of a slit.

pre.prompt: A "spooky" variation of the third (quantum) segment of Wave-particle duality.ogv occurs when the signal is so weak that only one particle is usually near the slit at any given time. This experiment was first performed by
options: Davisson and Germer in 1925.
Newton in 1704.
Taylor in 1909.
Aspect in 1982.
Young in 1801.

pre.prompt: A two-state quantum system has been coupled to its environment until it has fully dephased. How is its state best described?
options: A coherent superposition of the two states with a definite relative phase.
A classical (incoherent) mixture, in which the system is in one or the other state with probabilities |α→|2 and |α←|2.
A superposition whose relative phase has been measured.
The original pure state, because the probabilities of the two outcomes are unchanged.
pre.explanation: Adapted from LibreTexts, Essential Graduate Physics — Quantum Mechanics (Likharev), 10.1 "Quantum measurements": the density matrix is "gradually reduced to the diagonal form describing a classical mixture of two probability packets". Answer key per https://phys.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Quantum_Mechanics/Essential_Graduate_Physics_-_Quantum_Mechanics_(Likharev)/10%3A_Making_Sense_of_Quantum_Mechanics/10.01%3A_Quantum_measurements

post.prompt: A free particle in three dimensions is in a superposition of momentum eigenstates. At t = 0 its momentum is measured, and the result is p = (ħ/L)(3, 5, 1). Which state describes the particle immediately after that measurement?
options: The same superposition of momentum eigenstates it had before the measurement.
The momentum eigenstate corresponding to the measured momentum.
An equal-weight mixture of all the momentum eigenstates.
No state, until a second measurement is made.
post.explanation: MIT 8.04 Spring 2013, Problem Set 8 solutions (1d): "Measuring pk = (3n, 5n, n)/L immediately collapses the wavefunction into the corresponding momentum eigenstate." Answer key per https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/8-04-quantum-physics-i-spring-2013/resources/mit8_04s13_ps8_sol/

post.prompt: A system is in a pure quantum state |α⟩ = Σj αj |aj⟩, where |aj⟩ are the eigenstates of an observable A with eigenvalues Aj. If A is measured, what is the probability of obtaining the outcome Aj?
options: αj
|αj|2
√|αj|
Σj |αj|2
post.explanation: Adapted from LibreTexts, Essential Graduate Physics — Quantum Mechanics (Likharev), 10.1 "Quantum measurements": "the j-th outcome probability equal to Wj = |αj|2". Answer key per https://phys.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Quantum_Mechanics/Essential_Graduate_Physics_-_Quantum_Mechanics_(Likharev)/10%3A_Making_Sense_of_Quantum_Mechanics/10.01%3A_Quantum_measurements

post.prompt: Two ensembles are prepared with the same two possible states and the same probabilities for each outcome. In one ensemble the two components are combined coherently; in the other they form a classical mixture. Which experiment distinguishes the coherent ensemble?
options: Nothing can distinguish them: the two are identical in every experiment.
Counting how many systems are found in each state in a single measurement.
Interference between the two components, which the incoherent mixture cannot produce.
Measuring the total energy of the ensemble.
post.explanation: Adapted from LibreTexts, Essential Graduate Physics — Quantum Mechanics (Likharev), 10.1 "Quantum measurements": in the coherent stage "the coherence between the two component states → and ← is still preserved", while dephasing reduces the state to a classical mixture with no such coherence. Answer key per https://phys.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Quantum_Mechanics/Essential_Graduate_Physics_-_Quantum_Mechanics_(Likharev)/10%3A_Making_Sense_of_Quantum_Mechanics/10.01%3A_Quantum_measurements
